name: Dark Ages Character Creation (Faith and Fire)

pages.name: Dark Ages Character Creation (Faith and Fire)

text.content:
Dark Ages Character Creation (Faith and Fire)

Faith and Fire uses the same Trait-based Mind's Eye Theatre framework as modern-nights Laws of the Night, but with a distinctly medieval flavor and several mechanical differences worth noting for Storytellers running both eras side by side.

Quick Character-Creation Process

  1. Inspiration: Choose a concept, a Nature and a Demeanor, a clan, and a Road.
  2. Attributes: Prioritize Attribute categories (seven Traits primary, five secondary, three tertiary), then choose individual Traits.
  3. Advantages: Choose five Abilities, four Basic Disciplines (three at start, taken in order within each Discipline; a fourth becomes available through Free Traits), and five Backgrounds.
  4. Last Touches: Assign Blood Traits (by Generation), Willpower, seven Virtue Traits, a Morality/Road rating (the average of Conscience/Conviction and Self-Control/Instinct, rounded up), an optional derangement, Negative Traits and Flaws, and spend five (or more) Free Traits, including any Merits.
  5. Spark of Life: Narrative background, secrets, motivations, appearance, equipment, and quirks.

Attribute and Ability Priority

Unlike some modern chargen variants, Faith and Fire assigns Traits by strict priority rather than a flat pool: seven Traits in your primary Attribute category, five in your secondary, and three in your tertiary. Traits may be taken multiple times in the same descriptor to denote exceptional depth in one quality.

Virtue and Road Traits

Every character receives seven Virtue Traits split among Conscience/Conviction, Self-Control/Instinct, and Courage (every vampire has Courage regardless of Road). Each category must have between one and five Traits. Your starting Road rating equals the average of your Conscience/Conviction and Self-Control/Instinct Traits, rounded up.

Trading Road for Free Traits: During character creation only, a character may voluntarily lose one Road Trait in exchange for two Free Traits. This can be done only once, and counts as taking two Negative Traits for the purpose of the Free Trait economy. This option does not exist in the same form in modern-nights Laws of the Night chargen and represents the harsher, more fatalistic tone of the Dark Medieval setting.

Free Traits

A beginning character has five Free Traits, plus one additional Free Trait for each Negative Trait or derangement taken (maximum five Negative Traits, no more than three in any single Attribute category; one derangement, or two for Malkavians). Free Trait costs:

  • One Free Trait: an additional Attribute Trait.
  • One Free Trait: an additional Ability Trait.
  • One Free Trait: an additional Background Trait (Storyteller approval).
  • One Free Trait: a specialization in an Ability already possessed (one specialization per Ability).
  • Three Free Traits: an extra Willpower Trait, to a maximum of 10 permanent Willpower.
  • Three Free Traits: access to an in-clan Basic Discipline; six Free Traits for an in-clan Intermediate Discipline (Storyteller approval).
  • Two Free Traits: an extra Virtue Trait (this does affect total Road Traits).
  • Three Free Traits: an extra Road Trait.
  • Merits: variable Free Trait cost per the individual Merit.

Merits and Flaws

Merits and Flaws are organized into Physical, Social, Mental, and Supernatural categories. A character may take up to seven Traits total in Merits and up to seven Traits total in Flaws (elder characters may be permitted more Flaws by the Storyteller, reflecting the toll of age). Merits are purchased with Free Traits; Flaws grant Free Traits equal to their listed value.

Negative Traits and Derangements

Each Negative Trait taken grants one Free Trait, to a maximum of five Negative Traits (no more than three in a single Attribute category). A derangement counts as two Negative Traits (granting two Free Traits) and only one may be taken at character creation, except Malkavians, who begin with one derangement automatically and may take one additional one under the normal rules.

Blood, Generation, and Willpower

Most new vampires in the Dark Medieval begin at the Twelfth Generation, one generation higher on average than typical modern-nights starting characters (commonly Thirteenth Generation in modern LARP chargen), reflecting how young the vampire population of the era still is relative to the elders who walk it. Blood Pool maximum, Ability Trait maximum, and Willpower maximum all scale with Generation exactly as in the standard Generation chart used in modern nights. Characters begin with a minimum permanent Willpower appropriate to their Generation and may raise it further using Free Traits or Experience.

Experience Costs (Dark Ages-specific notes)

The baseline Experience costs for Attributes, Abilities, Backgrounds, Disciplines, Willpower, Virtues, and buying off Negative Traits or Flaws match those used in modern-nights Laws of the Night chronicles (see this system's Experience & Advancement Costs reference). Two Dark Ages–specific notes apply:

  • New Road Trait: Raising a Road/Morality Trait with Experience costs 2 Experience per Trait, requires Storyteller approval, and should reflect a substantive change in the character's ongoing story — identical in cost to raising Humanity/Path Traits in modern nights, but framed as growth in devotion to one's Road rather than a shift in Humanity.
  • New Merit bought to overcome an existing Flaw: As in modern nights, buying a new Merit or buying off a Flaw during play costs double the Trait's listed value in Experience, worked into the character's ongoing story with Storyteller approval. Faith and Fire explicitly calls out that a Merit may be purchased specifically to narratively overcome an existing Flaw at this doubled cost.
